text: Your water bottle is empty and you are thirsty, so can you explain why you need water using because?
I need water because I am thirsty.
Now you and two friends have empty bottles, so can you begin with We and explain the same need for all three of you?
We need water because we are thirsty.
Mia has no water to drink, so can you fix one word in the sentence about her need?
She needs water because she is thirsty.
You must write now but have no pencil, so can you explain why you need one using because?
I need a pencil because I must write.
Sam already has games but likes another one, so can you explain his wish using because?
Sam wants a game because he likes it.
You and a friend are both hungry and have no food, so can you explain your need using because?
We need food because we are hungry.
The rain starts and you open your umbrella, so can you tell us when you use it?
I use my umbrella when it rains.
Now the umbrella belongs to Mia, so can you change the sentence to tell us about Mia in the rain?
She uses her umbrella when it rains.
In this story, you use a bike to get to the park, so can you fix one word in the sentence?
I use my bike when I go to the park.
Pretend you travel to the park by bike, and tell us when you use your bike using when.
I use my bike when I go to the park.
When the rain starts, Sam opens his umbrella, so can you tell us about Sam and his umbrella using when?
He uses his umbrella when it rains.
Pretend you use a pencil for drawing, and tell us when you use it using when.
I use a pencil when I draw a picture.
In this story, you have eggs and milk every day, so can you tell us both what you eat and what you drink?
I eat eggs and drink milk every day.
Now Sam has the same food and drink every day, so can you change the sentence to tell us both things about him?
He eats eggs and drinks milk every day.
Mia has water every day, so can you fix the sentence about her daily drink?
Mia drinks water every day.
In this story, you have rice and water every day, so can you tell us both what you eat and what you drink?
I eat rice and drink water every day.
Lily has bread and milk every day, so can you tell us about both her daily food and drink?
She eats bread and drinks milk every day.
You and Sam have apples and water every day in this story, so can you tell us both things using We?
We eat apples and drink water every day.
May gives apples to Paul and gets money from him, so what does May do?
May sells apples.
Look at the same sale from Paul's side: he gives money and gets apples, so what does Paul do?
Paul buys apples.
Leo gives money and gets milk, so can you fix the action word in the sentence?
Leo buys milk.
Sara gives toys to Ben and gets money from him, so can you tell us what Sara does?
Sara sells toys.
Tom gives money to Eva and gets books from her, so can you tell us what Tom does?
Tom buys books.
Pretend you are Sara, giving toys to Ben and getting money from him, and tell us what you do using I.
I sell toys.
The steps on the card are fly the plane, get paper, and fold the paper, so which step must you do first?
First, I get paper.
You have the paper and have finished folding your plane, so what do you do next?
Then, I fly the plane.
In this story, eating lunch comes after washing your hands and before washing your plate, so can you fix the order word?
Then, I eat lunch.
Mia has a pencil but no paper for her picture, so what does she do first?
First, Mia gets paper.
You have folded the paper for a card, and the next step is to draw before giving it to Sam, so what do you do next?
Then, I draw a flower.
Ben's plan is to wash an apple, cut it, and eat it, so what does he do last?
Last, Ben eats the apple.
Mia's team wins and she feels happy, so can you put her feeling and its reason in one sentence using because?
Mia is happy because her team wins.
Mia and Ben are on the winning team and both feel happy, so how can you change the sentence to talk about them together?
They are happy because their team wins.
Sam's own toy breaks and he feels sad, so can you fix the word about whose toy it is?
Sam is sad because his toy breaks.
Lily's kite breaks and she feels sad, so can you explain her feeling using because?
Lily is sad because her kite breaks.
Sam breaks Ben's toy and Ben feels angry, so can you explain Ben's feeling using because?
Ben is angry because Sam breaks his toy.
You and Mia are on the winning team and feel happy, so can you explain both your feeling and its reason using We?
We are happy because our team wins.
